publisher: City & County of San Francisco — Rent Board (sf.gov)
title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
verified_finding: 1.6% allowable increase 3/1/2026–2/28/2027; 60% of Bay Area CPI-U; once per 12 months; anniversary date; base-rent-only calculation, no rounding up; 30/90-day notice (+5 days mailed) and required notice contents; rate in effect on effective date; rent increase license; no rent charge for additional occupants; vacancy decontrol; worked examples.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco (sf.gov News, 2026-01-14)
title: Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 - 2/28/27 Announced
verified_finding: 1.6% for rent-controlled units effective 3/1/2026–2/28/2027; $2,000 × .016 = $32.00 worked example; prior period (3/1/2025–2/28/2026) 1.4%.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco (sf.gov News, 2024-11-19)
title: Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/25 - 2/28/26 Announced
verified_finding: 1.4% effective 3/1/2025–2/28/2026, based on 60% of the 2.4% Bay Area CPI-U increase posted Nov 2024 by BLS; prior period 1.7%.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco — Rent Board (sf.gov)
title: Current Rates, including Rent Increase, Relocation, Sec. Deposit
verified_finding: Rate table: 1.6% (3/1/2026–2/28/2027), 1.4% (3/1/2025–2/28/2026), 1.7% (3/1/2024–2/28/2025); security deposit interest 4.2% for 3/1/2026–2/28/2027; historical '571 Allowable Annual Increases' schedule.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco (sf.gov)
title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory
verified_finding: Owners must report into the Housing Inventory and hold a current rent increase license before any annual or banked increase goes into effect; notice not enforceable without a license on the effective date.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco (sf.gov)
title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws
verified_finding: Many residential units built on or before June 13, 1979 have rent control AND just-cause eviction protection; post-6/13/1979 units, most single-family homes/condos exempt from rent limits; check building year via the Property Information Map.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco (sf.gov)
title: Evictions in San Francisco
verified_finding: Rent Board at 415-252-4600; tenants served an Unlawful Detainer should contact the Eviction Defense Collaborative at 415-659-9184 for free legal help.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco — Rent Board (sf.gov)
title: About Rent Board
verified_finding: Free phone/drop-in counseling 415-252-4600; Rent Board cannot arbitrate discrimination or retaliation — those go to the SF Human Rights Commission.

publisher: California Legislative Information (leginfo)
title: Civil Code § 827 — notice of rent increase
verified_finding: Statewide written-notice statute: at least 30 days for increases of 10% or less of the lowest rent in the prior 12 months; at least 90 days above 10%.

publisher: California Legislative Information (leginfo)
title: Civil Code § 1947.12 — Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) rent cap
verified_finding: Statewide cap: no more than 5% + regional CPI change, max 10%, in any 12-month period; max two increases per 12 months; exempts housing subject to a more restrictive local rent ordinance (SF Rent Ordinance qualifies); no limit on initial rent for a vacant unit.

publisher: California Legislative Information (leginfo)
title: Civil Code § 1946.2 — Tenant Protection Act just-cause eviction
verified_finding: AB 1482 just-cause eviction protections for covered tenancies.

publisher: California Legislative Information (leginfo)
title: Civil Code § 1954.50 et seq. — Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act
verified_finding: Statewide vacancy decontrol (owner may set initial rent for a new tenancy); exempts post-2/1/1995 construction and separately alienable single-family homes/condos from local rent caps; local ordinances otherwise remain in force.

publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. House (uscode.house.gov)
title: 42 U.S.C. § 3604 — Fair Housing Act prohibited practices
verified_finding: Federal law makes it unlawful to discriminate in the terms, conditions, or privileges of rental of a dwelling because of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, or disability (§ 3604(b)).

publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (hud.gov)
title: Fair Housing — HUD FHEO
verified_finding: HUD enforces the federal Fair Housing Act (42 U.S.C. §§ 3601–3619); seven federally protected classes.

publisher: Judicial Council of California (courts.ca.gov)
title: California Tenants — official guide (PDF)
verified_finding: For a fixed-term lease the landlord cannot raise rent during the term unless the rental agreement expressly allows it; AB 1482 cap 5% + CPI or 10% whichever lower; notice rules.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco — Rent Board (sf.gov)
title: Banked rent increases
verified_finding: A skipped annual increase is banked only if at least 24 full months pass without any increase; no limit on banked amount; banked increases do not expire, are added (not compounded/prorated), carry to new owners, and do NOT carry to a new tenant; banking allowed only since 4/1/1982; license + 30/90-day notice required.

publisher: City & County of San Francisco — Rent Board (sf.gov)
title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
verified_finding: Increases beyond the annual allowable amount require a Rent Board petition/passthrough (capital improvement, operating & maintenance, comparable-rent special circumstances, Prop I history, utility passthrough, bond passthrough worksheets); tenant need not pay until approved.

publisher: SF Planning Department (sf.gov PIM)
title: Property Information Map
verified_finding: Official tool to look up a building's year built / certificate of occupancy to confirm rent-control coverage.

publisher: Contra Costa County Housing Authority (government housing authority)
title: AB 1482: The California Tenant Protection Act of 2019
verified_finding: For increases effective 8/1/2026–7/31/2027 the applicable CPI is 3.8%, so the AB 1482 maximum is 8.8% (5% + 3.8%) for the SF-Oakland-Hayward region; restates § 1947.12 rules. NOTE: not the operative cap for SF rent-controlled units (S10 exemption).

publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (bls.gov)
title: Consumer Price Index (CPI-U)
verified_finding: Publisher of the CPI-U data the SF Rent Board and AB 1482 use in their formulas.
